review: round 1: source and behavioral review, updated after comparator edge-case audit
findings: Inventory matching is read-only and sums equivalent stacks independent of entry order or network stack splitting.
Entry identity includes BaseId, normal extra-data metadata, and the full custom enchantment effect payload; magic equipment is compared separately.
Initial 3D setup and ownership reconciliation skip SetActorInventory only when the local copy matches the authoritative owner snapshot.
Different counts, worn state, item metadata, custom enchantment effects, or spells still use the existing reconciliation path.
No item-count clamp, inventory deletion, engine offset, hook, or memory layout was introduced.
Two pure tests cover split/reordered stacks, worn-state changes, and custom enchantment differences.
scope: The incremental change from the tested corpse5 package is an inventory-equivalence helper, its use at two remote NPC snapshot application points, tests, and version metadata.
limitation: This source hypothesis is not confirmed by a game test. The user reports that the duplicate count predates the corpse5 second-kill/search workaround.
